verdict.rationale: Databricks documents a broad workspace-level REST API with per-operation reference, plus an official CLI and Python SDK for automation, and says Unity Catalog objects are managed through Catalog Explorer, SQL, the CLI and REST APIs. Nothing in the pack claims complete UI-to-API parity, and a community report notes there is 'no good way to get usage info programmatically', a concrete programmatic gap. missing for 10: an explicit documented UI/API parity guarantee, evidence that AI/BI dashboards, Genie and other UI-first features are fully API-addressable, a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: This reference contains information about the Databricks workspace-level application programming interfaces (APIs).
This reference describes the types, paths, and any request payload or query parameters, for each supported Databricks REST API operation.
You work with the objects Unity Catalog governs through Catalog Explorer, SQL, the Databricks CLI, and REST APIs.
The Databricks CLI (command-line interface) allows you to interact with the Databricks platform from your local terminal or automation scripts.
you learn how to automate Databricks operations and accelerate development with the Databricks SDK for Python
